title: SSP-4.1 — Exact Collection Planner And Receipt Evidence
summary: record the configured Analysis Works collection, exact parent and child Copy planning, metadata decisions and current receipt boundary
content_html:
SSP-4.1 — Exact Collection Planner And Receipt Evidence

Outcome

SSP-4.1 is complete at its review gate. analysis/works now exists as a flat lifecycle-owned editorial collection with the Analysis parent default of non-viewable source, an empty public projection, normalized Folder/Work/Series reading, and no assignable authoring-subject group. Copy planning resolves exact parent or child source and target collections; collection-aware apply, result navigation, and browser surfaces remain stopped at later SSP-4 stages.

Implemented Boundary

  • Copy planning inventories the exact configured collection root, supports all four parent/child source-target shapes and same-parent different-child Copy, rejects the same exact collection, rejects child descendant requests and internal child hierarchy, and blocks hierarchical input to a flat child target.
  • A public parent remains ineligible as a write target while an eligible configured child can accept a planned non-viewable copy. Media and build-source planning remain parent-scope-owned, and the receipt freezes the exact target rebuild owner and target-default viewability.
  • The analysis_tags customisation declares one typed non-subject group transfer contract. A matching target retains and validates it, an unsupported target records an omission, and a target that advertises the contract but rejects the configured value blocks preview. Shared folder_path, work_id, and series_id fields cannot be claimed by this custom transfer seam.
  • Receipt v2 records exact source and target collections, parent and collection configuration digests, document/media evidence, copied identities, custom-metadata and link decisions, media owners, target default, and rebuild owner. Restoration replans and compares the complete receipt; there is no v1 reader or compatibility alias.
  • Current parent-scope Copy and Move preview/apply behavior remains live. Copy apply rejects a child collection before mutation, Move accepts parent collections only, and no browser product module changed beyond updating its receipt-schema fixture.

Focused Evidence

  • 129 focused Python checks passed across exact collection planning, current transfer routes, parent Copy apply, Move apply, registered customisations, managed document targets, sub-scope building, checked scope configuration, and management capabilities.
  • The maintained document-transfer workflow module smoke passed against its current receipt v2 fixture, confirming the existing checked main-Index Copy/Move workflow still returns the opaque server receipt unchanged.
  • The collection matrix proves parent-to-parent, parent-to-child, child-to-parent, child-to-child, same-parent different-child, public-parent child eligibility, flat-child rejection, parent-owned media, internal and retained link decisions, target defaults, custom metadata retain/omit/reject, receipt restoration, and a no-write child apply guard.
  • A write-free plan against the checked analysis/tags and analysis/works configuration returned exact child identities, sub_scope_root placement, target_default_viewable: false, the analysis_tags group omission, receipt v2, and the exact analysis/works rebuild owner.
  • Explicit Python lint passed for the changed production and focused-test files. The empty Works source/manifests and lifecycle host revision validated, generated Analysis and browser projections rebuilt, public Works remained an empty manifest, and Analysis search contains no Works host entry.

Independent Review And Stop

The separate code/diff pass found no literal Projects-to-Analysis availability branch, title/route/row fallback, second transfer engine, scope-only receipt reader, custom field-name compatibility inference, subject interpretation, overwrite, lineage, publication trigger, Move expansion, or browser selection change. Exact collection resolution reuses the managed-target owner; the parent configs continue to own media and current apply behavior; the new customisation aspects remain code-owned and typed.

SSP-4.2 remains the owner of child document transformation, metadata omission during source rendering, parent/child link rewriting, media transfer, exact collection writes, coordinated child rebuild, result URLs, and full stale apply revalidation. Stop before SSP-4.2 approval.
